subject: Scaling control-plane glitch — reserved GPU pool impact and mitigation
messages:
From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@atlasai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: support@atlasai.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 503s and token errors during job window

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 503s and token errors for our Reserved GPU pool jobs around 07:45 PDT this morning. Affected jobs are timing out during model load and some inference requests return 503 / "kv cache miss" style errors. This is impacting several batch jobs and one real-time route we use for previews.

Quick details:
- Customer org: AtlasAI (account id: A-1129)
- Affected routes: /v1/generate-preview (high priority), batch inference pipelines (lower concurrency)
- First observed: 07:45 PDT; peak error rate ~07:55–08:05 PDT

Can you confirm whether this is on your side and whether there's a mitigation we can apply from our end? We're happy to pause some long-running batch jobs if that helps.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Wright
Head of Platform Reliability, AtlasAI
sam.wright@atlasai.com

Subject: RE: Spike in 503s and token errors during job window

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick heads up and sorry for the disruption.

Summary of immediate actions were taking (short term):
- We have paused one lower-priority batch queue assigned to your reserved pool to free capacity.
- Were temporarily routing /v1/generate-preview traffic to warmed fallback hosts in a different zone to reduce request failures while we investigate.
- Our SREs are collecting kernel logs, autoscaler traces, and the control-plane allocation timeline.

Would you be able to keep the live preview route traffic level steady (avoid bursts) for ~60 minutes while we stabilize? If you prefer, we can route a percentage of traffic to your dedicated fallback model variant instead of the cross-zone hosts — I can set that up now.

Ill follow up with a technical summary and a proposed remediation plan within 90 minutes.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage — reserved-pool allocation delay

Internal update (for SRE / infra):

What we see so far:
- Autoscaler observed node shortage and sent allocation requests at 07:46 PDT.
- Control-plane allocation service (rp-alloc) queued requests; a cache invalidation race caused a lookup to return stale pool metadata for ~12s, delaying instance assignments.
- During that window the front-end continued to accept requests; requests were routed to hosts that had partial model state (KV cache cold) leading to 503s and explicit "kv cache miss" errors in logs.
- Instance spin-up eventually completed, but the warmup path for KV cache was throttled by concurrent leader election in the pool, extending the impact window.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- We forced a control-plane cache refresh and accelerated instance assignment for AtlasAI's reserved pool.
- Warm fallback routing enabled for /v1/generate-preview.
- Paused low-priority batch queues to reduce queuing pressure.

Next actions (post-incident):
- Root cause: race in rp-alloc cache invalidation + warmup throttling in the allocator.
- Short-term engineering fix: add stronger cache-coherency checks and extend warmup concurrency for reserved pools (targeted PR today, rollback safe).
- Medium-term: instrument allocation latency metrics in the console per-reserved-pool, add an autoscaler circuit-breaker to avoid accepting requests to partially warmed hosts.

Assigning follow-ups:
- Ben to lead PR and coordinate canary (JIRA-INF-7921).
- Marissa to draft customer-facing timeline and credit proposal.
- Kimberly to confirm routing and coordinate customer comms.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: incident_timeline.pdf (initial timeline notes)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@atlasai.com>, contracts@atlasai.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Root cause & immediate remediation for AtlasAI reserved pool impact

Hi Sam — quick update with more detail and next steps. Thanks again for flagging this so we could act quickly.

What happened (short summary):
- At 07:46 PDT our control-plane allocation service experienced a cache invalidation race while processing autoscaler assignment requests for reserved pools. This produced a ~12s window where new instances were not correctly attributed to your pool. Front-end requests routed to partially warmed hosts resulted in 503s and cache-miss errors while the KV caches were rebuilt.

Impact observed:
- Error spike persisted ~07:45–08:05 PDT.
- Peak failure rate: ~18% on /v1/generate-preview; batch job retry rate increased and several long-running pipelines were delayed by 8–14 minutes.

Immediate remediations we performed for AtlasAI (completed by 08:15 PDT):
- Forced control-plane cache refresh and expedited node assignment for your reserved pool.
- Enabled cross-zone warmed fallbacks for priority routes.
- Paused low-priority batch queues attached to the same pool.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering patch to eliminate the race (Ben) — rollout to canary cluster tonight, full rollout pending results (JIRA-INF-7921).
- Console instrumentation (Marissa) — add per-pool allocation latency chart and alerting rule (ETA 2 weeks).
- Compensatory credit proposal: Marissa is preparing a draft with calculation and recommended credit. Well propose a credit commensurate with the observed processing delay and error impact; see attached spreadsheet for preliminary numbers.

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf (detailed timeline), atlas_charge_credit_calc.xlsx (preliminary credit calc)

We appreciate your patience — please let us know if you want additional technical detail or prefer a short call to walk through the timeline and credits.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
